warnings.warning: Equation 1 omits an explicit one-milliwatt unit in the denominator and leaves the input symbol P generic, although the intended 100 W to 50 dBm conversion is inferable.
Equation 2 typesets both antenna gains as tt terms and requires signed negative loss L, while Equation 22 renames the gains G and adds positive-looking path-loss formulas.
Equation 3 uses ell although the nomenclature lists A for the apparent straight-path role; the angle convention is not redefined at the formula.
Equation 5 cannot be reproduced from the printed paper because the altitude/path function y(x), its derivative, and numerical quadrature are not specified.
Equation 8 supplies x-coordinate scalars as P_in and P_out even though Equation 5 labels them as path points.
Equation 9 uses Theta prime while nearby prose/nomenclature also uses Theta_j; the turning height and real-path/escape branch are not closed.

Equation 10 reuses k for a refractive constant after nomenclature assigns k to absorption; e^2/(epsilon_0 m) is not approximately 80.5 without the missing frequency-conversion factor, and f_v=f/[k sec(phi_0)] is dimensionally suspect.
Equation 11 combines quantities described in kilometres while nomenclature labels B in metres; Equation 14 requires B and wavelength in a common unit.
Equations 12-13 do not define how the ray geometry yields surface distance D or state radian and longitude-wrap conventions.
Equation 14 returns a positive loss magnitude but Equation 22 adds L_free to received power without an explicit negative sign.
Equation 15 compresses spatially varying electron density and collision frequency into S times k and omits the kilometre-to-metre conversion and path-integration rule.
Equation 16 represents an entire patch by height standard deviation and does not retain correlation length, illuminated footprint, or slope distribution.
Equation 17 is called an amplitude factor and then squared again in Equation 19; the Gaussian roughness exponent convention is not derived or validated.
Equation 18 selects perpendicular polarization although the assumptions say no polarization is assigned; material constants also omit frequency, temperature, salinity, and uncertainty conditions.
Equation 19 sends complex rho directly into a real logarithm and does not explicitly use magnitude squared, so the reflected-power calculation is not mathematically closed.
The reflected-vector mean is unweighted by projected area or energy; deleting negative-z vectors is not a terrain visibility or shadowing test.
The 180 dB total budget, 170 dB allowable loss, 10 dB margin, and Summary wording are not reconciled in a per-hop component ledger.
The controller reports absorption, escape, and below-margin termination but publishes no thresholds, maximum-iteration guard, or per-hop trace for the observed two-hop maximum.

global_organization_chain: local reflection and recursive state update
parallel ocean land and coastal experiments

main_argument_chains.claim: A surface-hop decision requires a full propagation state.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain a connected trajectory-loss-direction recursion instead of an isolated reflection formula.
support_steps: Ionosphere loss changes power remaining at the surface.
Surface loss and direction determine the next hop.
The budget is reevaluated after every interaction.

main_argument_chains.claim: Communication feasibility is a thresholded resource ledger.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Output the last viable location, distance, and bounce count with a component ledger.
support_steps: Convert source and antenna terms to a common logarithmic budget.
Accumulate free-space, absorption, and reflection terms.
Stop when the remaining margin falls below 10 dB.

main_argument_chains.claim: The ray path is a recursive interface rather than a one-shot geometry.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Feed location and direction back into the next hop until a terminal branch occurs.
support_steps: Use IRI density to bend the ionosphere segment.
Compute a global landing point.
Use mesh normals to produce the next bearing and elevation.

main_argument_chains.claim: Surface roughness affects both survival and dispersion.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Compare first-bounce power separately from total distance, bounce count, and spatial concentration.
support_steps: Height dispersion changes phase coherence.
Material response changes reflected power.
Local normals scatter the outgoing direction.

main_argument_chains.claim: Frequency and elevation define a working ridge with competing objectives.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Choose settings by the target metric and tested grid rather than calling one pair universally ideal.
support_steps: Bounce, distance, and absorption heatmaps share a diagonal feasible band.
Low-frequency/high-angle settings favor more bounces but shorter net distance.
Higher-frequency/lower-angle settings can extend distance while increasing loss risk.

main_argument_chains.claim: Coastal reception requires density and reliability, not only extreme range.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the first-bounce concentration as the more defensible operating region and extrema as bounded observations.
support_steps: Table 5 reports observed extrema.
Figure 18 separates a concentrated first bounce from dispersed second bounces.
The paper warns that dispersed bounces are inconsistent for a boat.

main_argument_chains.claim: Current validation is qualitative compatibility, not predictive calibration.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Label current evidence accordingly and require independent empirical or benchmark validation before deployment.
support_steps: Trajectory shape and skip range are sanity checks.
Greyline plots compare model outputs with expectations.
Future Work asks for matched real contacts.

main_argument_chains.claim: A limitation becomes useful only when it closes into a verification plan.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use future work as an executable research backlog, not as evidence of current capability.
support_steps: Name the omitted time, terrain, footprint, phase, or hardware dimension.
Identify the new data and model interface.
Specify the measured contact record and output comparison.
